answer: One defense is to make influence depend on scarce, independently verified stake rather than the number of agent accounts. For example, agents can post a refundable bond and earn voting weight only after completing costly, randomly assigned tasks whose results are checked against external evidence. A sybil operator must fund and maintain each identity, while failed checks forfeit its bond; copying identities alone yields no extra influence. The crystal, grove, and ivory accounts still face the same per-agent cost.
